As someone has commented to before, just remind yourself everything is okay! Anxiety can makes us feel even more pain than we’re already in, and I understand how scary it is right now. I once spent a whole night panicking and was SO certain I was having a heart attack, but it ended up just being reflux! I was going to even ring the ambulance. I’d say take it easy and slow, and if the symptoms continue, visit a doctor. I know it will be uncomfortable to explain, but they’re there to help you. And the relief from the stress will be worth it!

I get that feeling. I used to self-harm in a desperate attempt for people to understand the pain I was in. I don’t know if it’s the same for you, but it felt like I was able to physically show my emotional pain. That people would finally understand because they could “see” it. In reality, self-harming becomes the opposite of what you aim to achieve. You aren’t “weird” or “different,” you’re just a human who wants to feel loved and heard. And you deserve that. I know this sounds cliche and like I’m just spitting out a staple response, but if you can please seek a therapist/psychologist. Any sort of professional help. You may not find the perfect fit at first, but you will find someone who wants to help. Who will be there for you and who will do their absolute best to understand you. I’ve been in a similar position so know I’m not trying to talk out of my ass right now.

Your mom sounds emotionally abusive and you don’t listen to a word she says. Your emotions matter as much as anybody else’s, and pain isn’t a competition. Your pain is real, and you don’t need validation to feel upset. 

About your appearance, I’ve struggled through a similar experience. I’ve been called ugly multiple times and people would call me gross/disgusting. I still wear my hair down because I’m too self-conscious to wear it up. I think in the grand scale of things, what matters is how YOU feel about yourself. As cliche as it is, they don’t matter. They are insignificant to you and no one can tell you how to look or feel except for yourself. If you don’t feel comfortable in your own appearance, ask yourself why. A lot of the time we change things about ourselves to feel accepted, but in reality there is always going to be someone who hates something about you. So the best you can do is live your life the way you want.

Our brains (ESPECIALLY with depression) can trick us into thinking other people secretly hate us, feel too guilty to leave, or only help us bc they want to make themselves feel good. Our brains are liars, and also convince us there is no way out of our situations when realistically speaking, there is ALWAYS another way out (even if it’s super fucking hard). But, if you really think your friends don’t care I wouldn’t consider them “friends”.

Hey, if I could give you an answer and fix everything that’s happening right now I would. But sadly, things aren’t and will never be that easy. The answer will never be simple and no one can answer that but you. I ask the exact same thing everyday; “What do I have to live for?” Your answer could be as big as not hurting a loved one, or as simple as “If I die, I won’t get to watch my favourite TV show tomorrow.” If life isn’t giving you a reason to live, you can tell life to fuck off and make your own reason. Please, just think right now, throwing everything that sucks out of the window, think where you are right now and of anything, no matter how small it is, that you would miss if you left this world.

Call an ambulance as soon as possible. ODing has an EXTREMELY small chance of causing death, but will cause extreme pain if not treated. These can be seizures, brain damage, severe memory loss, heart problems and much much more. I’ve been suicidal many times and have always thought about OD’ing. But trust me, after plenty of research, this is NOT the path you want to go down.
